key_insight: Quantum features help most when they add complementary information to classical features, rather than replacing them outright.
clinical_relevance: For cancer drug discovery workflows, this suggests quantum machine learning may be useful only if the representation and fusion strategy match the prediction target and data structure.
method: Built a classical-quantum multi-view framework that keeps the full classical input alongside simulated quantum features.
Compared concatenation and attention fusion against single-view, replacement, and masking controls.
Tested controlled synthetic targets and benchmark datasets to isolate when complementary views improve prediction.
evidence_signal: Across controlled experiments and benchmarks, fusion improved performance on several datasets, but classical baselines still led on some tasks and results depended on representation choice and available views.
watch_item: The study uses simulated quantum features and mixed benchmark outcomes, so gains may not transfer universally and depend on careful representation selection.
paper_title: When do quantum views help? Complementary classical-quantum representations in multi-view fusion
